sample_unit: clinical scenarios (each answered by 4 chatbots and 21 board-certified thoracic surgeons)

links.outcome: Chatbot vs board-certified surgeon scores on board-style thoracic surgery scenarios
links.effect: Median score per scenario was 1.06 for chatbots vs 1.88 for surgeons (difference 0.66; P = .019); chatbots were worse in all but 2 scenarios.
links.quote: The median score per scenario was 1.06 for chatbots, compared to 1.88 for surgeons (difference, 0.66; P = .019).

links.outcome: Chatbot critical failures on board-style clinical scenarios versus surgeons
links.effect: Critical failures were more frequent for chatbots (median 0.50 per chatbot/scenario vs 0.19 per surgeon/scenario; P = .016).
links.quote: Chatbot answers were significantly more likely to be deemed critical failures compared to those provided by surgeons (median, 0.50 per chatbot/scenario vs 0.19 per surgeon/scenario; P = .016).

screen.reason: Empirical comparison of four commercial LLM chatbots against board-certified thoracic surgeons on ABTS board-style clinical scenarios, with no specific organizational deployment guardrails or practices tested.
